scope.description: One fault-free execution of a normally bootstrapped 3-node in-memory cluster with a small SnapshotInterval/SnapshotThreshold/TrailingLogs: warm traffic, isolation of one follower, further traffic so the leader compacts, reconnection so the follower recovers by InstallSnapshot, then a bounded idle window on the recovered node (isolated again so no further InstallSnapshot can occur) with the leader observed over the same window as control.
assumptions: MakeCluster(3) with SnapshotInterval=40ms, SnapshotThreshold=20, TrailingLogs=5 performs real bootstrap, replication, snapshots and log compaction through the in-memory transport.

Disconnecting only the chosen follower leaves the leader with a quorum (itself plus the other follower), so the cluster keeps committing and the leader's log compacts past the isolated follower's next index.
The isolated follower does not raise its term while isolated because pre-vote is active by default, so reconnecting lets the leader complete the recovery without a spurious election.
Isolating the recovered node again before the window removes the leader as a source of further snapshots, so any new snapshot in that node's store must be produced by its own snapshot goroutine.
Both observed nodes run the same configuration; the leader is idle in the window except for heartbeats.
excluded: Safety claims: no state-machine divergence, lost entry or double application is asserted.
Cost measurement: bytes written, disk wear and FSM Snapshot() latency are not measured.
Behaviour with MonotonicLogStore implementations, which take the removeOldLogs branch instead of compactLogs.
Duration of the condition under production SnapshotInterval values.

basis.prefix: The harness builds the prefix with the captured test facilities and real producers only: MakeCluster(3, conf) with SnapshotInterval=40ms, SnapshotThreshold=20 and TrailingLogs=5 bootstraps the cluster; leader.Apply() commits 60 warm commands so every node snapshots; the chosen follower is cut off with c.Disconnect and 140 further commands are committed by the remaining quorum so the leader's log compacts; c.FullyConnect reconnects and the follower recovers through the InstallSnapshot handler. The harness then emits recovery_state (snapshot index 202 above log store last index 62 in the local run) and disconnects the recovered node again before the observation window. window_start carries each node's snapshot index, newest snapshot ID, log store last index, last snapshot index, should_snapshot() and applied index; during the window the harness samples each node's snapshot list every 40ms counting distinct IDs; window_end reports distinct_snapshot_ids, snapshot_created_without_new_entries (derived as distinct>=2 and applied index unchanged, with both operands emitted), newest snapshot ID and index, log store last index, should_snapshot() and applied_delta. No storage is pre-filled and no production code is modified.
basis.requirement: On a server whose log store last index sits below its last snapshot index, the automatic snapshot condition computes the delta between the log store index and the snapshot index as an unsigned subtraction without an ordering guard, so the condition stays true while the server is idle and its snapshot goroutine keeps creating fresh snapshots at the same index.
basis.responsibility: shouldSnapshot's delta computation between the log store's LastIndex and the last snapshot index, as consumed by runSnapshots to trigger takeSnapshot, for a server that recovered through InstallSnapshot and whose log store was not raised to at least the snapshot index.

comparisons.description: Recovered node: with no newly applied entries during the window, more than one distinct snapshot ID appears in its own snapshot store, i.e. fresh snapshots are created repeatedly at the same index.
Control: the leader in the same window, with the same idle condition and its log store at or above its snapshot index, does not create further snapshots.
